VERDICT: LGTM

The change slots into the codebase's established pattern exactly and introduces no catch-all or duplication.

- `Owner.salutation(String, String)` joins the family of deterministic static derive/compose methods on `Owner` (`contactPreference`, `checkDigit`, `ageBand`, …), with the same Javadoc shape documenting null/blank handling. Keeping the pure composition logic on the model and off the mapper matches its siblings.
- `OwnerMapper.formatSalutation(Owner)` mirrors the sibling `format*` methods precisely: null-check the owner, then delegate to the static `Owner.salutation(...)`. It's placed next to the other formatters and wired via the same `@Mapping(expression = ...)` idiom. (The one formatter that computes inline, `formatDisplayName`, is the outlier; delegating to the model is the dominant convention here, so this is the right choice.)
- The `title` field, getter/setter, Bean Validation `@Pattern`, controller assignment, the four DB schema columns, and the openapi request/response additions are all standard Spring/JPA wiring placed where a maintainer would expect them.

Logic is in the right unit and nothing is duplicated.
